$comment: Canonical machine-readable verification-suite registry (M00-W04, spec §8.5). Consumed and schema-validated by scripts/verify.py. Suite STATE is derived at runtime: ACTIVE suites run their commands and must pass; a suite with an activation condition is NOT_YET_APPLICABLE while every listed activation package is still NOT_STARTED or READY in docs/PROJECT_STATUS.md, and becomes REQUIRED_MISSING (a hard failure) as soon as any activation package has begun (IN_PROGRESS or later) while the suite's discovery globs still match no files. Nobody flips a boolean by hand: state follows the project-status tables. Proof names refer to typed discovery-proof implementations in scripts/verify.py; commands are argv arrays executed from the repository root with no shell.

suites.name: Pinned-toolchain assumptions
suites.explanation: Fails fast when the active Node, pnpm, Python, uv, or Rust toolchain does not match the repository pins (.nvmrc, packageManager, .python-version, [tool.uv] required-version, rust-toolchain.toml).

suites.name: Formatting (Prettier + Ruff format + rustfmt)
suites.explanation: Check-only; never rewrites files. Canonical docs are excluded from Prettier by .prettierignore.

suites.name: TypeScript lint (typed strict ESLint)
suites.explanation: Python lint (Ruff) is owned by the python suite and Rust lint (Clippy) by the rust suite so command ownership stays unambiguous; pnpm verify runs all three.

suites.name: Typechecking (tsc all TS projects + strict mypy)
suites.explanation: Covers every TypeScript workspace package, the root Playwright/e2e project, and strict mypy over Python services and the verification runner. Turborepo caching is sound here because turbo.json globalDependencies hashes tsconfig.base.json (base-config edits invalidate cached typechecks); test execution is separately cache-bypassed with --force.

suites.name: TypeScript unit tests (Vitest via Turborepo)
suites.explanation: --force bypasses the Turborepo cache so discovery counts always come from fresh Vitest executions; every workspace package that declares a test script must actually run and report at least one passing test.

suites.name: Generated-contract integrity (drift check)
suites.explanation: ACTIVE since M01-W02 (Generate TypeScript and Python contracts) began: scripts/generate-contracts.ts regenerates the deterministic TypeScript and Pydantic v2 trees from packages/contracts/schemas/ into an isolated temporary directory and byte-compares the COMPLETE committed inventory under packages/contracts/generated/ — missing, stale, modified, and unexpected extra files all fail with actionable paths, and the check never modifies the working tree. This is distinct from the 'contract' suite below: contract-gen proves committed generated artifacts are exactly reproducible from the canonical schemas, while 'contract' runs cross-language compatibility tests (owner M01-W05). If the generator files at scripts/generate-contracts.* ever disappear while M01-W02 remains started, this suite returns to REQUIRED_MISSING and pnpm verify fails. No hand-maintained generated files may be introduced to satisfy it (spec §1.5).

suites.name: Synthetic development fixture corpus
suites.explanation: ACTIVE when M02-W01 begins; since M02-W02 the focused surface is the combined m02-w01 and m02-w02 suites. Fails closed on an empty focused inventory, deterministic seed drift, schema/version/hash/reference/consistency defects, real-looking PII or secrets, deprecated corrected-platform v1 producer references, scanner bypass, any skipped/todo/pending/excluded outcome, or any discovered-test count other than the separately authored test-layer exact 165.

suites.name: Cross-language contract tests
suites.explanation: ACTIVE since M01-W05 began. One versioned, hash-locked synthetic corpus drives the canonical strict Ajv/generated TypeScript path, generated Pydantic v2 path, and a private test-only Rust harness built --locked --offline. The suite proves bounded protocol execution, normalization, representative round trips, version behavior, authorization/default-deny escalation, hostile raw-wire rejection, historical compatibility mutations, infrastructure failure propagation, and deterministic non-empty discovery. It does not expose production Rust contracts or claim coverage beyond the committed representative set.

suites.name: Browser end-to-end tests (Playwright, pinned Chromium)
suites.explanation: Runs every discovered Playwright test (currently the browser-infrastructure smoke test). Discovery is proven with `playwright test --list` as one of the suite's proofs (evaluated with the run itself; an empty discovered set fails the suite); forbidOnly in playwright.config.ts rejects focused tests; no external sites are contacted. Future product e2e specs are added under e2e/ without changing this command contract.

suites.name: Visual regression tests
suites.explanation: NOT_YET_APPLICABLE: no renderable product surface exists — the first spec-mandated visual-regression owner is M10-W06 (document validation snapshots); desktop-view and extension-panel snapshot layers attach with their own milestones by updating this entry. There is deliberately no placeholder snapshot or pixel test: that would be a mocked success (spec §1.5). When M10-W06 begins, this suite turns REQUIRED_MISSING and pnpm verify fails until real visual specs exist under e2e/visual/.

suites.name: Python quality and tests (Ruff + mypy + pytest via uv)
suites.explanation: Uses the repository-pinned interpreter (uv-managed 3.12.13) and == pinned tools. pytest exit code 5 (no tests collected) is treated as a hard failure, never success.

suites.name: Rust format, lint, tests, build (pinned toolchain)
suites.explanation: Explicit --manifest-path keeps execution independent of the caller's working directory; rust-toolchain.toml pins 1.97.1. The native-host scaffold remains fail-closed and is built independently. M01-W05 also formats, lints, tests, and builds its private compatibility harness --locked --offline; this adds test evidence only and no native-host runtime behavior or production Rust contract API.

suites.name: Platform-portability policy (three-OS CI and shared scripts)
suites.explanation: Read-only, fail-closed static validation that required CI keeps the exact macos-15/windows-2025/ubuntu-24.04 matrix running the identical canonical doctor/verify commands, SHA-pinned official actions, read-only permissions, no continue-on-error or masked child failures, frozen/locked installs, exact toolchain probes, isolated uncached RUSTUP_HOME, an allowlisted dependency-cache set, failure-only Playwright artifacts, and that shared runtime scripts/package commands stay platform-neutral (no /tmp//bin//usr literals, shell=True, Bash-only wrappers, POSIX permission-bit dependence, case-colliding tracked paths, or missing LF enforcement).

suites.name: Requirements and work-package traceability
suites.explanation: Read-only, fail-closed validation of the exact v1.4 193-requirement and 300-work-package inventories, immutable v1.2/v1.3 reviewed hash layers, the M00-W11-reviewed v1.4 mapping/dependency hashes, explicit M00/M01/M27 dependencies, four critical-gate effects, honest UX/provider states/evidence, deterministic generated view, and next-work derivation.

suites.name: Project-status validation
suites.explanation: Structural validation of the canonical project-memory files; its failure fails pnpm verify.

suites.name: Repository-integrity checks
suites.explanation: Built-in checks: all v1.4 canonical project-memory files exist; the canonical spec is one regular non-symlink file with no case/Unicode/content variant; lockfiles exist for every active ecosystem; every required root script exists and is not a no-op; tracked text has no prohibited raw C0 bytes; no passWithNoTests-style bypass in tracked config; no focused (.only) or skipped (.skip / @pytest.mark.skip) tests outside allowed_skips; pnpm verify is status-neutral (git status --porcelain identical before and after).
